The unifying signal across all clinical medicine specializations is people impact as the primary motivation paired with science passion — clinical practitioners apply scientific knowledge directly to human health outcomes, making both the scientific foundation and the human service orientation essential qualifications.

Remote workEnvironment penalty and solo collaboration penalty reflect a structural reality: clinical medicine requires physical examination, procedural intervention, and therapeutic relationship that cannot be replicated asynchronously or in isolation.

As a field-level profile, this intentionally sits between the high people-and-hands_on emphasis of nursing-and-allied-health and the high analytical-and-discover emphasis of biomedical-and-research; specialization profiles sharpen differentiation between GP breadth, specialist precision, and emergency urgency.

The field is defined by the hands_on + people combination at near-equal high weights — nursing and allied health practitioners deliver care through direct physical intervention, patient assistance, and therapeutic touch rather than primarily through diagnosis or research.

Routine workStyle at supporting (higher than clinical-medicine field) reflects the shift-based, protocol-driven nature of care delivery: medication schedules, care plan cycles, and therapy programs operate on structured repetitive cadences that organized, consistency-oriented users will find rewarding rather than constraining.

Money goals at weak (vs supporting in clinical-medicine) captures the compensation reality — impact and balance are the primary motivational drivers that sustain practitioners in demanding but comparatively lower-compensated nursing and allied health roles.

Communication co-leading with people at strong is unique in the healthcare domain at field level — mental health and psychiatry practitioners work through language and therapeutic relationship as the primary clinical instrument rather than physical examination or laboratory investigation.

Ideas passion at strong alongside social is the clearest differentiator from clinical-medicine and nursing-and-allied-health — practitioners engage with theoretical frameworks (CBT, psychodynamic, attachment theory) as genuine intellectual content, making conceptual curiosity about human behavior a real fit signal.

Building passion penalty and build workStyle penalty separate this from biomedical-engineering and health-informatics — the output is qualitative human behavioral change measured over therapeutic time horizons, not constructed systems or deployed tools.

Discover impact at maximum and science passion near the ceiling define the field — biomedical and research practitioners are motivated by generating new knowledge about biological systems and disease rather than applying existing knowledge to direct patient care.

Solo collaboration at strong and help workStyle at penalty are the sharpest contrast with clinical-medicine and nursing-and-allied-health — research relationships are peer and mentor-based within lab groups rather than continuous direct patient service interactions.

Math at double-strong subjects alongside science differentiates this field from clinical medicine pathways — biomedical research requires statistical modeling, bioinformatics, and quantitative experimental design that clinical practitioners rarely encounter at comparable depth.

Field-level profile anchored on ideas passion + analytical + communication co-leading — strategy and consulting roles are intellectually demanding environments where synthesizing ambiguous information into structured recommendations is the primary professional value creation.

Penalty on routine workStyle and balance goals reflects the inherent variability of consulting engagements: new client contexts, shifting project scopes, and deadline-driven deliverable cycles structurally conflict with predictable cadences and sustainable working hours.

Differentiates from operations-and-logistics at field level by leading with ideas (not building) in passions, by weighting discover impact at supporting rather than systems-only, and by keeping client_facing at strong supporting rather than a weak signal.

Field-level profile sitting between creative-dominant (brand-strategy) and analytical-dominant (digital-marketing) specializations — communication and creativity co-lead at strong, with analytical at supporting, ensuring users with mixed profiles score here before being routed to specialization pathways.

Science penalty in passions and writing leading in subjects differentiates this field from strategy-and-consulting at field level — marketing practitioners engage with audience behavior and cultural narrative rather than organizational systems and economic models.

Watching as a learning preference at supporting (unique among business domain fields) reflects the culture-consumption dimension of marketing work: practitioners who stay current in the field actively engage with media, campaigns, platform trends, and creative work as professional development, not just entertainment.

Systems impact at the maximum and organized as primary strength defines this field — operations and logistics practitioners design and optimize the invisible mechanical structures that move goods, services, and information at scale; reliable system performance is the only meaningful output measure.

Differentiates from strategy-and-consulting at field level by leading with organized (not analytical) and building passion (not ideas), reflecting the execution-first orientation: operations roles implement and sustain systems rather than formulating the strategic rationale that precedes them.

No outdoor workEnvironment penalty at field level (unlike technology) because warehouse management, distribution center operations, and port logistics involve meaningful physical environment work — the penalty appears selectively in desk-bound specializations like supply-chain-management but not across the whole field.

Variety goals at maximum is unique in the entire business domain — entrepreneurship is structurally defined by role ambiguity; founders wear every hat simultaneously across product, sales, finance, and operations, making variety-aversion a fundamental mismatch with the daily experience of building a company from scratch.

Fast_learning as co-primary strength (highest in the business domain alongside e-commerce-entrepreneurship) reflects the compressed learning arc: founders must develop enough competency across unfamiliar domains fast enough to make consequential decisions before running out of runway.

Balance at penalty is deliberately calibrated — the early-stage entrepreneurship lifestyle is structurally incompatible with fixed working hours and low-stress evening routines; practitioners who strongly prioritize personal stability should route toward management roles in established organizations rather than founding paths.

Field-level profile with people impact at maximum and the highest people + communication strength pairing in the business domain — people and organisation roles exist to develop human potential, manage organisational culture, and build workforce capability as the primary professional output.

Teaching at supporting learningPreference (uniquely high in the business domain) signals that practitioners in this field are naturally drawn to knowledge transfer, skill development, and coaching as intrinsically motivating activities rather than purely instrumental ones.

Science penalty in passions and build penalty in workStyle separate this field from strategy-and-consulting and operations-and-logistics — people practitioners work through relationship influence, policy design, and organisational development rather than quantitative analysis or system construction.

Field-level profile defined by analytical dominance and money goals at maximum — investment and markets roles are the most financially incentivised in the business domain, where quantitative edge, speed of information synthesis, and risk-adjusted decision-making are the primary value-creation mechanisms.

Discover and systems impact both present captures the dual orientation: markets professionals uncover pricing inefficiencies and arbitrage opportunities (discover) while operating within structured financial system infrastructure (systems).

Balance penalty at strong weight captures the structural reality across the field — trading desks, investment banking divisions, and asset management teams operate under market hours, earnings cycles, and deal deadlines that make lifestyle predictability consistently incompatible with peak performance.

Field-level profile anchored on people + communication leading — the sharpest differentiator from investment-and-markets is that financial planning practitioners are fundamentally in service relationships with individual clients over long time horizons rather than analysing markets or executing deals.

Help workStyle at maximum and client_facing at dominant reflect the fiduciary reality: every analytical output (portfolio review, tax strategy, estate plan) is organised around serving a specific named individual's life goals.

Balance goals at supporting (highest in the finance domain) reflects that fee-based advisory practice structures and AUM-based recurring revenue create more sustainable working patterns than deal-contingent or market-hours-dependent finance roles.

Balance at strong goals is the highest in the finance domain and a deliberate differentiator from investment-and-markets — risk and insurance practitioners work within regulated frameworks, structured actuarial review cycles, and defined underwriting protocols that create genuinely predictable working patterns.

Systems impact at maximum captures the field's orientation: risk management outputs are frameworks, policies, and models that operate at organizational and portfolio scale rather than individual transaction outcomes.

Field-level profile sits between the consumer-facing relationship model of financial-planning-and-advisory and the pure-quantitative orientation of investment-and-markets — differentiation sharpens at the insurance-and-risk-management specialization level.

Watching as primary learning preference is the defining differentiator within the creative-arts domain at field level — visual designers develop craft through active consumption of visual culture, design history, and contemporary work rather than through reading theory or structured courses.

Arts at maximum subject alongside music passion at strong captures the multi-sensory aesthetic orientation that defines the visual design practitioner: colour relationships, compositional rhythm, and typographic voice are internalized through broad cultural exposure not limited to the visual alone.

Differentiates from media-and-production at field level by stronger solo collaboration and build workStyle at supporting — visual designers produce discrete artefacts through focused solitary craft rather than through the multi-person collaborative production processes that characterize film, audio, and live media work.

Music passion at the highest weight in the creative-arts domain field profiles reflects that all media-and-production specializations — film, audio, podcast, social, game design — engage with sound, music, and temporal rhythm as foundational craft elements even when the primary output is not audio.

Large_team at supporting (uniquely elevated in the creative-arts domain) captures the production-team reality: film sets, recording studios, and live broadcast operations require coordinated multi-role crews rather than the solo or small-team structures that characterize static visual design.

Solo collaboration penalty separates this field from visual-design and writing-and-content — media production is structurally collaborative; practitioners who strongly prefer solitary work will find the crew-dependent, coordination-intensive, and schedule-driven nature of production work continuously friction-generating.

Arts and math at double-strong subjects is the defining combination in the creative-arts domain — architecture is the only creative profession that requires equal technical rigour in structural physics, building code compliance, and environmental systems alongside aesthetic composition and spatial narrative.

Systems impact at supporting (unique among creative-arts field specializations) reflects the built infrastructure reality: buildings are occupied, maintained, and regulated systems that must perform structurally, environmentally, and functionally across decades of use, not just aesthetic objects.

Client_facing at supporting (the highest in the architecture cluster) captures the client-brief, design-review, and planning-approval cycles that structure the professional project lifecycle — architectural practice is client-commissioned work requiring sustained relationship management through years-long project timelines.

Reading passion at maximum weight is unique in the entire creative-arts domain — writing careers require voracious reading across genres, periods, and forms as continuous professional development; practitioners who do not read widely do not develop the stylistic range and tonal awareness that distinguish publishable from unpublishable work.

Solo collaboration at maximum and remote workEnvironment at primary reflects the structural reality that writing at its core is a sustained solitary cognitive practice — drafting, revision, and editorial cycles are incompatible with open-plan collaboration, and the best writing environments are ones where practitioners have uninterrupted control over their time.

Balance goals at supporting (uniquely high in the creative-arts domain) reflects that established freelance and staff writer positions offer more predictable working patterns than performance-contingent creative careers in visual design or media production — editorial calendars and commissioning cycles create a degree of rhythm absent from project-based creative work.

Express and people impact at maximum/near-maximum co-leading is unique at field level in the creative-arts domain — performing arts practitioners exist to transmit emotional experience through live presence to audiences in shared physical space; the human witness relationship is non-negotiable and cannot be asynchronously replicated.

Remote penalty is the strongest in the creative-arts domain — performance is definitionally live and embodied; practitioners whose work quality is unaffected by remote conditions are not performing artists in the primary sense.

Community collaboration at supporting (the highest in the creative-arts domain) captures the ensemble, company, and scene dimensions: performing artists belong to artistic communities, training cohorts, and professional networks where shared development, peer feedback, and collective identity formation are core to professional growth.

variety goals scoring high is a deliberate differentiator — users who strongly prefer depth and specialization will score comparatively higher on pure frontend or backend; full-stack rewards breadth-first motivation.

arts subject leads with math firmly supporting, reflecting the dual demands of visual interface design and platform-specific constraints (memory management, OS APIs, performance budgets) that require real technical depth.

hands_on is supporting rather than weak because device testing, gesture interactions, and debugging on physical hardware give mobile development a tactile feedback loop absent from purely web-based roles.

Penalty on people strength, help workStyle, and client_facing collaboration reflects the highly technical, protocol-focused nature of work where user-facing relationship skills are a structural mismatch with daily responsibilities.

science passion scores as strong rather than supporting (unlike other dev tracks) and money goals score high — both reflect the high-stakes, financially-incentivized, cryptography-rooted culture of the blockchain ecosystem.

ideas passion co-leading with tech at strong level is unique to this specialization among dev tracks — XR developers must envision entirely new spatial interaction paradigms, making speculative thinking as critical as implementation skill.

lab workEnvironment scores as primary (over remote) because hardware rigs, device testing, and spatial calibration make this one of the few software specializations with genuine lab and physical testing requirements.

express impact at supporting level distinguishes XR from other build-first specializations — the output is an immersive experiential artifact, not just a functional system, making expressive motivation a meaningful positive signal.

Penalty on analytical strength, math subject, and analyze workStyle is the sharpest score separator from backend/data paths — these users actively prefer visual workflow-driven tools precisely to avoid the complexity that analytical roles demand.

science passion penalty and balance goals at supporting level reflect users who want to build functional products fast without engineering prerequisites; impact and growth dominate over money, aligning with the indie-maker and business-operator culture of the ecosystem.

The strongest math + science double-strong in the AI/data cluster: ML engineering is fundamentally research-adjacent, requiring genuine mathematical fluency in linear algebra, probability, and calculus — not just API usage.

build remains a supporting workStyle (not just analyze) differentiating this from data-science — ML engineers train, serve, and optimize models in production, making implementation skill genuinely relevant alongside pure research.

Penalty on people strength, client_facing collaboration, and balance goals reflects long research cycles with uncertain outcomes and high cognitive load; users motivated primarily by human connection should route toward AI product management instead.

The sharpest differentiator from all other AI/data specializations is communication and writing leading as primary signals — prompt engineering is fundamentally about precise language construction and behavioral elicitation, not model architecture or statistics.

Penalty on building passion separates this from ML engineering — prompt engineers produce language artifacts and evaluation frameworks, not deployed code infrastructure; implementation-first users will find the output insufficiently tangible.

reading passion at supporting level is unique within the technology domain — prompt engineers internalize domain knowledge across many subjects to write effective few-shot examples and system instructions, making broad literacy a genuine fit signal.

Data scientists are defined by the analytical + discover combination — the core output is insight translated into decisions, not deployed systems or cleaned pipelines, making communication a genuine supporting strength rather than weak as in ml-engineering.

Penalty on routine workStyle reflects the exploratory, hypothesis-driven nature of data science: open-ended analytical work with uncertain outcomes contrasts with the structured cadences of data-analysis and data-engineering.

reading passion at supporting (uniquely present in the AI/data cluster) captures that data scientists engage extensively with research papers, domain literature, and statistical methodology — intellectual breadth is a real fit signal.

The defining cluster is organized + build + systems — data engineers construct the reliability infrastructure that data scientists consume, making correctness, SLA adherence, and pipeline throughput the tangible daily outputs over insight generation.

routine workStyle at supporting is uniquely high in the AI/data cluster — data engineers run scheduled ingestion jobs, monitor pipeline health, and maintain SLAs on cadenced delivery schedules rather than pursuing open-ended investigation.

Differs from backend-development by elevating science passion to supporting and keeping discover impact at supporting level, reflecting domain knowledge requirements around data formats, statistical distributions, and query execution plans.

The sharpest differentiator within AI/data: people impact leads over discover, and client_facing collaboration dominates — analysts serve business stakeholders by answering defined questions on predictable schedules rather than pursuing open-ended research.

writing subject at supporting (uniquely high in the data cluster) reflects that compelling narrative presentation of findings is as measurable an output as the analysis itself; dashboard clarity and executive summaries are core deliverables.

routine workStyle at supporting (higher here than in data-science) captures weekly dashboards, monthly business reviews, and regular reporting cadences that structure most analyst roles — predictability of workflow is a real feature, not a limitation.

systems impact at maximum weight is the defining signal — DevOps/platform engineers exist to make shipping reliable and fast; uptime, deployment frequency, and pipeline throughput are the tangible outputs, not user features or analytical insights.

routine workStyle at supporting is the highest in the technology domain after data-analysis — on-call rotations, monitoring cadences, incident runbooks, and release checklists create genuine operational rhythm that structured-preference users will find rewarding.

Differentiates from cloud-architecture by leading with organized (not analytical) as co-primary strength and keeping create impact low — DevOps implements delivery infrastructure, it doesn't design the architectural patterns it operates within.

ideas passion co-leading with tech at strong is the sharpest differentiator from devops-platform-engineering — architects spend material time evaluating tradeoffs, designing topology diagrams, and selecting technology before any implementation begins.

Penalty on routine workStyle captures that cloud architects are hired precisely for non-routine judgment: technology selection, cost optimization modeling, and failure domain design are decisions made rarely but with lasting consequence.

client_facing collaboration at supporting (highest in the infra cluster) reflects the stakeholder advisory reality of senior architecture work — cost reviews, governance presentations, and capability briefings to engineering leadership are regular responsibilities.

discover impact at strong and creativity at supporting strength are unique in the infrastructure cluster — offensive security and pen testing require adversarial creative thinking to locate non-obvious attack surfaces that automated scanners miss.

Differentiates from cybersecurity-analysis by penalizing routine workStyle and balance goals — active security work (red teaming, vulnerability research, incident response) is inherently unpredictable, reactive, and incompatible with structured operational cadences.

lab workEnvironment at supporting (higher than in devops/cloud) reflects hands-on malware analysis, exploit development in sandboxed environments, and CTF-style challenges that characterize skill development and professional practice in this track.

The key differentiator from cybersecurity is routine workStyle at supporting and office environment leading — SOC analysts work structured shifts, triage alerts from SIEM dashboards, and follow established incident runbooks, making predictable cadence a feature rather than a friction point.

Penalty on create workStyle is the sharpest scoring separator from active security — analysts respond to detected events rather than engineering novel attack or defense mechanisms; creation-first users will find reactive monitoring unsatisfying.

writing subject at supporting (higher than in cybersecurity) reflects the documentation burden of analyst work: incident reports, threat intelligence briefs, and chain-of-evidence records are formal, regular deliverables that demand clear technical prose.

The only infrastructure specialization where people impact leads and client_facing collaboration dominates — sysadmins are the human face of IT operations, resolving user issues at service desks, managing onboarding hardware, and communicating system status to non-technical staff daily.

balance goals at strong is unique in the infrastructure cluster and reflects the more predictable working conditions of sysadmin roles relative to on-call DevOps and incident-responsive security tracks; structure and sustainability are genuine role features.

Penalty on create workStyle separates this from DevOps and cloud paths — sysadmins maintain and respond within existing systems rather than engineering new delivery infrastructure; creation-first users will feel constrained by the operational scope.

math and science both at double-strong subjects is shared only with ml-engineering in the technology domain — embedded work requires signal processing, memory architecture, real-time OS scheduling, and electronics fundamentals that demand genuine scientific fluency.

Penalty on remote workEnvironment is the clearest differentiator from software development tracks — hardware-in-the-loop debugging, oscilloscope analysis, and physical sensor calibration require lab presence; fully remote embedded engineering is not viable.

hands_on at supporting strength (highest in the software-development cluster alongside mobile) reflects the physical tactile reality: burned-out microcontrollers, soldering iron work, and device flashing give embedded development a material engagement absent from web-based roles.

people impact co-leading with create at near-equal weights is the defining differentiator from graphic design and frontend — UX designers are user advocates whose prototype, research finding, and interaction flow outputs are explicitly measured against human behavioral outcomes, not aesthetic production alone.

social passion at strong (uniquely high in the technology domain cluster) captures the genuine interest in human behavior, social dynamics, and interaction patterns that separates authentic UX practitioners from technically-adjacent roles who pick up design tooling.

Penalty on solo collaboration reflects a structural reality: UX without user testing, stakeholder critique, and design review sessions is methodologically broken — isolation is not a work style preference but a discipline failure mode.

science passion penalty cleanly separates from ai-product-management — general PMs are motivated by user impact and market strategy, not by the mechanics of model architectures or data pipeline constraints; deep technical curiosity routes to the AI variant.

Penalty on solo collaboration and routine workStyle reflects that product management has no meaningful solo or repetitive version — the role is entirely constituted by meetings, negotiations, prioritization debates, and stakeholder context-sharing.

Differentiates from product-management by elevating tech and science passions to strong/supporting and making analytical a genuine third-tier strength — AI PMs must credibly engage with evaluation design, model limitations, and data pipeline constraints, not just roadmap strategy.

analyze workStyle leading over help (reverse of product-management) reflects the additional technical translation burden: AI PMs regularly interpret model performance metrics, prompt behavior, and latency/cost tradeoffs for non-technical stakeholders.

fast_learning at supporting strength (higher than standard PM profile) reflects the structural reality that AI capabilities shift faster than any product domain in history — an AI PM who stops upskilling becomes strategically irrelevant within months.

writing subject at maximum weight (0.945) is unique across the entire technology domain — technical writing is the only specialization where prose quality is the primary measurable output rather than code, design artifacts, or strategic decisions.

reading passion at strong (uniquely primary in the technology domain) reflects that excellent technical writers are voracious readers who internalize documentation patterns, API reference styles, and domain knowledge across multiple engineering disciplines.

Penalty on building passion is the cleanest differentiator from developer paths — technical writers translate and clarify systems built by others; users whose primary motivation is constructing things will find the documentation cycle creatively unsatisfying.

organized and analytical at near-equal strong weights is unique in the product-and-design cluster — QA engineers maintain structured test suites, track defect regression rates, and follow systematic verification protocols where documentation discipline directly determines team release confidence.

discover impact at supporting (highest in the product-and-design cluster) captures the adversarial mindset that defines skilled QA work — finding edge cases and failure modes before production is a genuine source of professional satisfaction, not just a task completion.
